studentWritten.text:
Assume √5 is rational in the form of p/q (q ≠ 0)
√5 = p/q (Here, p & q are integers and they are coprime)
5 = p²/q² (square both the sides)
∴ p² = 5q² — (1)
If a prime no. p divides q², then p must divide q.
∴ p = 5c (c is another integer) — (2)
Substitute 2 in 1
25c² = 5q²
q² = 5c²
From the above, 5 divides p² and q²
Then p and q have a common factor of 5.
Hence, this contradicts our assumption, and therefore √5 is irrational.
